name: Oral SARMs
method: HMTc Method v2.0 — no-regulatory-anchor (control) form. Government-limit lookup returns nothing for this class, so cells resolve to `control` or a substantiated `not_material`; ICH Q3D / USP <232> route-appropriate PDEs are toxicological anchors only, never product-content limits.
governing_basis: No lawful product heavy-metal content limit exists for this unapproved-drug class; the Method v2.0 ceiling term is absent and the occurrence term is firewalled staff-only. Every cell is `control` (test + method + toxicology-anchored escalation, no number) or a substantiated `not_material`. ICH Q3D / USP <232> route-appropriate PDEs are toxicological anchors only, never product-content limits.
scope_note: Selective androgen receptor modulators supplied as oral capsules, tablets, or liquid droppers, sold as research chemicals outside any drug-approval or supplement framework. The oral route carries the larger per-gram toxic-metal burden in the seed evidence (Craven 2025: oral nickel mean 27.48 ug/g, near the 200 ug/day oral PDE depending on dose; oral aluminium mean 651 ug/g), so the escalation anchor is the oral ICH Q3D PDE.
certification_scope: Heavy-metal SAFETY only. HMTc does not endorse, approve, or vouch for the efficacy or legality of these products.
reference_method: ICP-MS per USP General Chapter <233> (or an equivalently validated ICP-MS / ICP-OES elemental method) on the finished product in its as-sold form: total-element quantitation for the eight totals (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Sn, Al, total Cr), with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on an elevated total-arsenic result and reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation on an elevated total-chromium result.

seed_evidence_disclaimer: Occurrence measurements (e.g. Craven 2025) are recorded as category-opening context and to justify that each analyte is material; per the Part 2 / Part 19 firewall they are NOT converted into a published product-content limit for this class.

Pb.reference_method: ICP-MS per USP General Chapter <233> (or an equivalently validated ICP-MS / ICP-OES elemental method) on the finished product in its as-sold form: total-element quantitation for the eight totals (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Sn, Al, total Cr), with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on an elevated total-arsenic result and reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation on an elevated total-chromium result.
Pb.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a lawful product heavy-metal content limit for this unapproved-drug class, so the Method v2.0 min(percentile, ceiling) rule loses its ceiling term and the occurrence (percentile) term is a firewalled staff quantity that must not be published as a product-content limit. HMTc therefore controls lead by mandatory testing rather than a published concentration number: every certified lot is quantified by the reference method, and the result is judged against the route-appropriate toxicological anchor below, not against a fixed ug/kg cap. The absence of any regulatory backstop is precisely why an independent heavy-metal-safety mark carries its highest consumer-protection value for this class.
Pb.escalation: Escalation is toxicological, not a fixed concentration. Using the product's labeled or manufacturer-directed single dose and maximum daily dosing, the measured lead concentration is converted to an implied elemental daily intake (ug/day) and compared to the oral ICH Q3D / USP <232> permitted daily exposure. A result whose implied daily intake reaches or exceeds that PDE is an automatic certification failure. Tier-1 analytes carry zero tolerance for PDE exceedance (Status C or worse immediately); Tier-2 analytes are eligible for the Status B transitional band (up to 150% of the anchor, with a documented remediation plan) before failure. Any detection above the method reporting limit — even well below the anchor — triggers a documented source investigation and a repeat-lot verification, because a contaminant present at all in a synthetic product signals an uncontrolled raw material, catalyst, or reagent.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation, source, or reaction pathway in the abiotic synthetic manufacture of peptides, SARMs, anabolic-androgenic steroids, or research chemicals. Methylmercury is produced by microbial biomethylation in aquatic and sediment environments and enters the human food supply through marine bioaccumulation; there is no biomethylation step in chemical synthesis, purification, or reconstitution. Any mercury contamination of these products is inorganic or elemental mercury introduced by reagents, catalysts, or apparatus, and is fully captured by the total-mercury (tHg) control cell. ICH Q3D itself sets the mercury PDE on inorganic mercury as the worst case for pharmaceutical elemental impurities, confirming that inorganic, not organic, mercury is the relevant species for a manufactured product. This is a no-pathway determination (absence of a formation route), corroborated by the total-Hg control that bounds any organomercury fraction.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury quantitation by ICP-MS (the tHg control); no methylmercury speciation is defined for a synthetic product with no biomethylation pathway.

tox_anchor.basis: chronic dietary intake reference (mg/kg body weight/week)
tox_anchor.note: No government sets a per-product oral aluminium content limit outside the lone FSANZ infant-formula entry, so the oral anchor is the intake-based tolerable weekly intake. Craven 2025 measured oral-AAS aluminium at mean 651 ug/g (up to 1220 ug/g), the single highest toxic-metal load in the survey; at gram-scale oral dosing this can consume a large share of the tolerable weekly intake. The intake reference anchors the escalation rule and is not a product-content limit. Toxicological anchor for the escalation rule only; NOT a product-content limit.
